documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 31F, positive home tests, LMP 12/21/22 — about 7 wks. Planned? "Not exactly, but we're happy." No bleeding, no cramping. On PNV with iron, ferrous sulfate TID, calcium BID.
OB hx: two term cesareans (2019, 2021). Family hx of note: mother with previa/C-section, maternal aunt with uterine rupture in labor.

O: Vitals reviewed, wt 88.0. Comfortable. Abd soft, nontender, healed low transverse scar.
Urine hCG positive in office.

A/P:
1. Intrauterine pregnancy, ~7 weeks, high risk given two prior cesareans and obesity — referral placed to high-risk OB at the regional hospital; she prefers to deliver there. Early ultrasound and prenatal labs per OB.
2. Iron deficiency anemia — CBC today. Continue iron and PNV.
3. Bleeding or pain: L&D or ED, not here. She understands.
Will let OB take the lead on prenatal care; she will keep us posted.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin 11.4, a touch lower than October but fine for early pregnancy. Keep the iron going. The OB office should call you within the week; let us know if they don't.

documents.title: High-risk obstetrics intake letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional Hospital — Department of Obstetrics, High-Risk Clinic

Re: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992
Visit date: 03/14/2023

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the referral. Ms. Perez was seen today for her new obstetric visit at 11 weeks 6 days by LMP of 12/21/2022, consistent with today's dating ultrasound, which showed a single live intrauterine pregnancy.

Obstetric history: G3P2, two low transverse cesarean deliveries (2019, 2021). Medical history: iron deficiency anemia on oral iron, obesity. Allergies: sulfa drugs. Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily.

Given two prior cesareans she is not a candidate for a trial of labor, and we have recommended a planned repeat cesarean delivery; timing will be scheduled later in the pregnancy. Family history of uterine rupture in a maternal aunt was noted and discussed. Prenatal labs drawn today. She will be followed in our clinic every 4 weeks.

We will keep you informed.

Sincerely,
Attending Obstetrician, High-Risk Clinic

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 09/20/2023 07:35

CC: abdominal pain, pregnant

HPI: 31 yo G3P2 at 39w0d by LMP with two prior low transverse cesareans, brought in by spouse with abrupt severe abdominal pain beginning about two hours before arrival. Pain is continuous and getting worse. Denies vaginal bleeding or loss of fluid. Followed by the hospital's high-risk OB clinic; repeat cesarean planned.

PMH: iron deficiency anemia, obesity. PSH: cesarean x2.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: VS stable on arrival (see flowsheet). Visibly distressed, guarding. Abdomen: fundal tenderness with voluntary guarding. Pelvic (with OB at bedside): presenting part has moved up — head was engaged at the last prenatal visit and is now higher in the pelvis.
Bedside ultrasound: cephalic (vertex) presentation.
Toco/FHR: recurrent late decelerations with reduced variability; contractions irregular and weakening in strength.

MDM: findings concerning for uterine rupture in a patient with two prior uterine scars. OB emergently consulted and assumed care; patient taken directly to the OR.

Dispo: admitted to Obstetrics.

documents.title: Operative Report — emergency cesarean
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date of surgery: 09/20/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: suspected uterine rupture at 39 weeks, nonreassuring fetal heart tracing, two prior cesareans.
Postoperative diagnosis: uterine rupture.
Procedure: emergency laparotomy, repeat cesarean delivery, repair of uterine rupture.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

Findings: uterine rupture confirmed at laparotomy. Liveborn infant delivered and handed to the neonatal team; admitted to the NICU.
The rupture was repaired in layers with good hemostasis. Tubes and ovaries normal. Abdomen closed in standard fashion.
No transfusion. Counts correct. Patient to PACU in stable condition.

documents.title: Obstetrics Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admitted 09/20/2023, discharged 09/24/2023.

Diagnoses: uterine rupture during labor at 39 weeks; abnormal fetal heart rate tracing complicating labor; status post emergency repeat cesarean with repair of rupture; iron deficiency anemia; obesity.

Course: presented to the ED with acute abdominal pain at term and taken emergently for cesarean delivery with repair of the uterine rupture. Postoperative course without complication. Tolerating diet, ambulating, pain controlled on oral medication. Hemoglobin 9.1 on postoperative day 3; not transfused. Infant in NICU, followed by the neonatal team.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily; NEW ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.

Counseling: patient counseled that any future pregnancy carries high risk of repeat rupture and should be followed by maternal-fetal medicine with early planned delivery.

Follow-up: OB postoperative check 2 weeks; primary care within 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Spouse call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt's husband called (verbal OK on file) to let Dr know Gladys had an emergency C-section yesterday at the regional hospital, "something about the uterus tearing." She is recovering on the maternity floor, baby in NICU. Asked what follow-up she needs here. Told him we will request the hospital records and call her when she's home. Message to PCP.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call. Pt home since Sunday 9/24. Incision pain controlled with ibuprofen, using it 2-3x/day. No fever, no wound drainage, bleeding is light. Walking around the house. Taking iron TID and PNV. Baby still in NICU, she visits daily. Hospital records received this morning and routed to PCP. Follow-up booked with PCP Tues 10/3.

conditions.label: Abnormality in fetal heart rate and rhythm complicating labor and delivery

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 13 days after emergency cesarean for uterine rupture at 39 wks (regional hospital, admitted 9/20-9/24). Discharge summary and op note reviewed.

S: Sore at the incision but improving, ibuprofen once or twice a day now. Lochia light. No fever. Tired — up at night, back and forth to the NICU, baby expected home soon. Mood "okay, a lot happened fast." Taking ferrous sulfate TID, PNV, calcium. OB post-op check is Thursday.

O: Wt 91.4 kg. Vitals reviewed. Tired-appearing but comfortable.
Abd: low transverse incision clean, dry, intact, no erythema, appropriately tender. Uterus not palpable above expected.
Lungs clear, heart regular. No calf tenderness.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P:
1. S/p emergency laparotomy, cesarean and repair of uterine rupture — healing well. Rupture repaired; marking resolved on our list. Hospital counseled her about the risk in any future pregnancy; she heard it. OB to follow.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, worse after delivery (Hb 9.1 at discharge) — CBC and iron today. Continue ferrous sulfate TID.
3. Mood — PHQ-9 low. Lots of support at home. Reviewed warning signs; she knows to reach out.
4. Flu shot today.
Follow up after the holidays, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Post-hospital labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin is 9.6, a little up from the 9.1 at discharge, and your iron stores are low again (ferritin 8) after the surgery, which is expected. Keep taking the iron three times a day with food if it bothers your stomach. We'll recheck in a few months.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 32F, LMP 1/1/24, ~6.5 wks. Uterine rupture with emergency cesarean and repair 9/20/23 — less than 5 months ago. She is worried and wants to do everything right this time. No bleeding, no pain. On PNV, ferrous sulfate TID, calcium.

O: Wt 88.5. Vitals reviewed. NAD. Abd soft, nontender, incision well healed.
Urine hCG positive.

A/P:
1. Pregnancy after recent uterine rupture repair — high risk. Urgent referral to maternal-fetal medicine at the regional hospital rather than general OB; RN to call their office today. Reinforced: any abdominal pain, bleeding or "popping" feeling = call 911/go to L&D.
2. Iron deficiency anemia — Hb and iron today. Continue iron and PNV.
3. Will coordinate with MFM; asked her to sign release so we get their notes.

documents.title: Blood count and iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is 10.1 and ferritin 12 — still low but better than October. Keep the iron going. Maternal-fetal medicine has the referral and should call you by Tuesday.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine, Regional Hospital
Consultation — 03/19/2024
Patient: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992
Referring: primary care

Reason: pregnancy following uterine rupture.

Ms. Perez is a 32 year old G4P3 at 11 weeks 1 day by LMP and first-trimester ultrasound (single live intrauterine pregnancy). Her third delivery, in September 2023 at this hospital, was an emergency cesarean for uterine rupture at term with repair of the uterus. Prior low transverse cesareans 2019 and 2021. Medical: iron deficiency anemia on oral iron; obesity.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily.

We discussed the substantially increased risk of recurrent rupture, including before labor, and the warning symptoms. Plan: MFM co-management with high-risk OB, serial growth ultrasounds, and planned cesarean delivery ahead of labor; the date will be set in the third trimester. Strict return precautions given.

Thank you for involving us.
Maternal-Fetal Medicine Attending

documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 09/23/2024 06:50

CC: severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, 38 weeks pregnant

HPI: 32 yo G4P3 at 38w0d followed by MFM, history of uterine rupture repaired at emergency cesarean in September 2023 (plus two earlier cesareans). Felt something "pop" this morning, then abrupt severe abdominal pain and bleeding from the vagina. 

PMH: iron deficiency anemia, obesity, uterine rupture 9/2023. PSH: cesarean x3.
Meds: PNV with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

Vitals: BP 110/70, HR 102, T 37.2 C (99.0 F).
Exam: uterus tender, abdomen guarded. FHTs irregular, baseline about 110 bpm with minimal variability. No presenting part felt above the pelvis.

Labs: Hgb 10.2, Hct 30.4, plt 210K, WBC 12.0K.

MDM: presumed recurrent uterine rupture with fetal compromise. OB/MFM paged stat, to OR immediately.
Dispo: admit OB.

documents.title: Operative Report — emergency cesarean
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date: 09/23/2024
Pre-op dx: suspected recurrent uterine rupture, 38 weeks, abnormal fetal heart tracing.
Post-op dx: recurrent uterine rupture.
Procedure: emergency laparotomy, cesarean delivery, repair of uterine rupture.
Anesthesia: general.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

Findings: uterine rupture present on entry. Liveborn infant delivered, to neonatal team and NICU.
Uterine defect repaired in two layers, hemostatic. Adnexa normal. Fascia and skin closed.
No blood products given. Counts correct x2. To PACU stable.

documents.title: Obstetrics Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admission 09/23/2024 — Discharge 09/27/2024

Principal diagnosis: recurrent uterine rupture during labor at 38 weeks.
Other: fetal heart rate abnormality; anemia of pregnancy (admission Hgb 10.2); iron deficiency anemia; obesity; history of three prior cesareans.

Hospital course: emergency cesarean delivery with repair of the rupture on the day of arrival. Recovery uncomplicated. Hgb 8.8 on POD 3, asymptomatic, no transfusion. Infant cared for in the NICU.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Discharge meds: continue prenatal vitamin with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID; ibuprofen 600 mg q6h PRN pain.

Patient again counseled regarding the very high risk with any future pregnancy.
Follow-up: OB incision check 1-2 weeks; PCP 1 week for anemia.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after discharge Friday. Pain okay with ibuprofen. Incision dry. No fever, light bleeding only. PCP will check her blood count Wednesday. Baby in NICU. Records arrived today, routed. Appt Wed 10/2 confirmed.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM — second uterine rupture

Admitted 9/23-9/27 at the regional hospital: at 38 wks felt a pop, then pain and bleeding; emergency cesarean with repair of a recurrent rupture. Hgb 10.2 on arrival, 8.8 POD3, no transfusion. Records reviewed.

S: Sore but improving. No fever, incision fine, bleeding light. Baby still in NICU, doing well per pt. Taking ibuprofen a couple times a day, iron TID, PNV, calcium.

O: Wt 92.3. Vitals reviewed. Pale conjunctivae. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd: incision healing, no erythema or drainage. No edema.
PHQ-9: 5.

A/P:
1. S/p repair of recurrent uterine rupture — recovering. OB follows the incision. Resolve episode on our list.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, post-operative dip — CBC and iron today; continue ferrous sulfate TID.
3. Mood — PHQ-9 5, she says she is tired more than down. Will recheck.
4. Flu shot today.
RTC in a few months for anemia, then physical.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin 9.4 and ferritin 7. Low, as expected after the surgery, and a little better than the hospital's 8.8. Keep up the iron three times a day. Call us with any questions.
